headline: South Asia: CDF Munir says armed forces remain resolute in defeating terrorism, ensuring lasting peace: ISPR
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: CDF Munir says armed forces remain resolute in defeating terrorism, ensuring lasting peace: ISPR.
- Western Russia: Dnipro dealing with aftermath of Russian strike, railway network still under attack – Ukraine's Interior Ministry.
- Persian Gulf Region: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill three as Zelenskyy in US for UN summit.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Poll: Trump approval falls to record low of 32% as war continues.
- Military Times, 17 hours ago: Poll: Trump approval falls to record low of 32% as war continues.
Only 34% of respondents in a new Reuters/Ipsos poll said they approved of the strikes on Iran.
- Military Times, 17 hours ago: Airmen can’t get enough of new, warlike basic training, leaders say.
Six months after the Air Force launched a tougher, more combat-centric training program, airmen and prospective instructors are clamoring to get involved.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Escalating domestic violence impacting St James churches.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: Escalating domestic violence impacting St James churches.
WESTERN BUREAU: Domestic violence is emerging as an increasingly common issue confronting churches across St James, as pastors are routinely called upon to counsel people struggling with troubled relationships and family conflicts. The Reverend Godfrey Francis, secretary of the St James Ministers Fraternal, said the pressures of modern life, coupled with poor communication and weak conflict resolution skills, were helping to fuel the problem, leaving churches to confront the fallout.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: ‘I used to say, ‘Good job, police’, but now I feel it’.
Relatives of 35-year-old businessman Jordon Perry Smith took their grief and anger to the streets of Seaford Town, Westmoreland, on Monday, demanding answers over his fatal shooting during a police operation. The protest came three days after Smith was killed at his home in an incident police sources have described as a shoot-out, while his relatives continue to reject that account and accuse members of the Constabulary Force of executing him.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: CDF Munir says armed forces remain resolute in defeating terrorism, ensuring lasting peace: ISPR.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: CDF Munir says armed forces remain resolute in defeating terrorism, ensuring lasting peace: ISPR.
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir said on Tuesday that the armed forces remained resolute in defeating terrorism and ensuring lasting peace and stability, according to the military’s media wing. Field Marshal Munir made the statement while visiting Peshawar Corps Headquarters, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. He was received by the Peshawar Corps commander.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: Pakistan, 7 other Muslim nations call upon Israel to fulfil its commitment under Gaza plan.
Pakistan joined other Muslims countries on Tuesday in calling for Israel to “immediately fulfill its outstanding commitments” under the first phase of a plan aimed at ending the conflict in Gaza. The demand was made in a joint statement attributed to the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Egypt, Turkiye, Indonesia, Jordan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates after they met on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: Iran shows willingness to return to negotiating table.
• Naqvi meets Pezeshkian, Momeni to ‘discuss mediation process’ • Iran ‘grateful’ to Pakistan’s political, military leadership for peace efforts • US refuses visas to some members of Iranian president’s delegation • Second Qatari LNG cargo ship ‘cleared by Iranians’ due today ISLAMABAD: Iran on Monday indicated its willingness to return to dialogue with the United States to de-escalate tensions.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Security forces kill 6 terrorists in intelligence-based operation in Balochistan's Saran Tangi.
Six terrorists were killed and nine suspected individuals were arrested during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) by security forces in Balochistan’s Saran Tangi area, state-run Radio Pakistan reported on Tuesday. According to the report, the operation was conducted under ‘Operation Shaban-2’. “According to security sources, the operation was conducted against terrorists of Fitna al Hindustan on the basis of intelligence information,” it said.

The casualties occurred in Dnipro, he said, where people are still believed to be trapped under the rubble of a hit industrial facility. The missile had previously been associated with China’s larger Type 055 destroyers. Showing it fired from a Type 052D – a class the People’s Liberation Army has built in far greater numbers – suggests Beijing may be able to spread the weapon well beyond its much smaller force of Type 055s. India - bottom line: The Revisit: When WWI reached India as German ship bombed Madras.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: The Revisit: When WWI reached India as German ship bombed Madras.
On September 22, 1914, World War I reached India when the German cruiser SMS Emden shelled Madras, firing more than 125 shells in around 10 minutes. The attack set a Burmah Oil tank ablaze, damaged buildings and sent residents fleeing. This story revisits the dramatic raid, the Emden’s deceptive disguise, its mysterious retreat and how the German warship’s name became part of southern India’s vocabulary.

- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: China building new next-generation submarine as India's numbers stay constant.
Fresh satellite imagery of China’s Bohai Shipyard shows a submarine believed to be a possible Type 095 nuclear-powered attack submarine under construction. The vessel features an apparent pumpjet propulsion system and X-shaped stern, suggesting efforts to improve stealth, efficiency and manoeuvrability. The development has regional implications as Pakistan expands its submarine fleet with eight Chinese-designed Hangor-class AIP submarines, expected to raise its fleet to 11. India operates 16 conventional and three strategic submarines, but fleet expansion has been delayed.
